subtopics: History of microbiology — Koch's postulates, contributions of Pasteur, Lister, Jenner, Fleming
Classification of microorganisms — bacteria, viruses, fungi, parasites
Bacterial morphology — cocci, bacilli, spirochetes; cell wall structure (Gram-positive vs Gram-negative)
Bacterial growth — growth curve, culture media (simple, enriched, selective, differential, transport)
Bacterial genetics — transformation, transduction, conjugation, transposons, plasmids

Sterilization & disinfection — physical methods (autoclaving, hot air oven, pasteurization, filtration, radiation), chemical methods (glutaraldehyde, formaldehyde, chlorhexidine, alcohol, iodine, phenol)
Biofilms — formation, clinical significance
Normal flora — distribution, significance
Bacterial toxins — exotoxins vs endotoxins
Antimicrobial susceptibility testing — disc diffusion (Kirby-Bauer), MIC, E-test
Innate immunity — barriers, phagocytes, NK cells, complement, acute phase proteins, pattern recognition receptors (TLRs)
Adaptive immunity — humoral & cell-mediated
Antigens — types, epitopes, haptens, superantigens
Antibodies — structure, classes (IgG, IgM, IgA, IgE, IgD), functions, isotype switching
Complement system — classical, alternative, lectin pathways; MAC, C3a/C5a (anaphylatoxins), opsonization (C3b)
Complement deficiencies & associated diseases
MHC — Class I & Class II, antigen processing & presentation
T cells — CD4+ (Th1, Th2, Th17, Treg), CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, T cell activation
B cells — activation, germinal center reaction, plasma cells, memory cells

Hypersensitivity reactions — Type I (IgE-mediated, anaphylaxis, atopy), Type II (cytotoxic — transfusion reactions, HDN, autoimmune hemolytic anemia), Type III (immune complex — serum sickness, Arthus reaction), Type IV (delayed — tuberculin test, contact dermatitis, granuloma)
Autoimmunity — mechanisms, molecular mimicry, examples
Immunodeficiency — primary (SCID, DiGeorge, Bruton, CGD, Wiskott-Aldrich, selective IgA deficiency), secondary (AIDS, malnutrition, drugs)
Transplant immunology — types of grafts, rejection mechanisms, HLA typing
Tumor immunology — tumor antigens, immune surveillance
Vaccines — types (live attenuated, killed, toxoid, subunit, conjugate, recombinant, mRNA), national immunization schedule, cold chain
Immunological techniques — ELISA, Western blot, immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, RIA, complement fixation test, precipitation, agglutination (Widal, Coombs test)

Staphylococcus aureus — virulence factors (protein A, coagulase, toxins — TSST-1, exfoliatin, PVL, enterotoxins), diseases (skin infections, endocarditis, osteomyelitis, food poisoning, TSS, scalded skin syndrome), MRSA
Coagulase-negative staphylococci — S. epidermidis (prosthetic infections), S. saprophyticus (UTI)

Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) — virulence factors (M protein, streptolysin O & S, erythrogenic toxin), diseases (pharyngitis, scarlet fever, impetigo, erysipelas, necrotizing fasciitis, rheumatic fever, post-streptococcal GN), ASO titer
Streptococcus agalactiae (Group B) — neonatal meningitis, sepsis
Streptococcus pneumoniae — capsule (quellung reaction), diseases (pneumonia, meningitis, otitis media), optochin sensitivity, bile solubility
Viridans streptococci — S. mutans (dental caries), S. sanguis (subacute endocarditis)
Enterococcus — E. faecalis, E. faecium, VRE
Corynebacterium diphtheriae — diphtheria toxin (ADP-ribosylation of EF-2), Elek test, Albert stain, Schick test, pseudomembrane
Bacillus anthracis — anthrax (cutaneous, pulmonary, GI), Medusa head colony, bamboo stick appearance, McFadyean reaction
Bacillus cereus — food poisoning (emetic & diarrheal)
Clostridium tetani — tetanospasmin, lock jaw, risus sardonicus, opisthotonus, spatula test
Clostridium botulinum — botulinum toxin, flaccid paralysis, infant botulism
Clostridium perfringens — gas gangrene (alpha toxin — lecithinase), Nagler reaction, food poisoning, necrotizing enteritis
Clostridium difficile — pseudomembranous colitis, toxin A & B
Listeria monocytogenes — tumbling motility, cold enrichment, neonatal meningitis, granulomatosis infantiseptica
Actinomyces israelii — sulfur granules, cervicofacial actinomycosis
Nocardia — modified acid-fast, pulmonary nocardiosis
Neisseria meningitidis — meningococcal meningitis, Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome, capsular serotypes, chocolate agar, oxidase positive
Neisseria gonorrhoeae — gonorrhea, ophthalmia neonatorum, disseminated gonococcal infection, no capsule, no vaccine
Moraxella catarrhalis — otitis media, sinusitis, COPD exacerbation
Haemophilus influenzae — type b (meningitis, epiglottitis), X & V factor requirement, satellite phenomenon, Hib vaccine
Bordetella pertussis — whooping cough, pertussis toxin, Bordet-Gengou medium, lymphocytosis
Escherichia coli — pathotypes (ETEC, EPEC, EHEC/O157:H7, EIEC, EAEC), UTI, neonatal meningitis (K1 capsule), HUS
Klebsiella pneumoniae — lobar pneumonia (currant jelly sputum), mucoid colonies, ESBL
Salmonella typhi — typhoid fever (Widal test, blood culture, bone marrow culture), carrier state, rose spots, enteric fever
Non-typhoidal Salmonella — gastroenteritis, osteomyelitis in sickle cell
Shigella — bacillary dysentery, Shiga toxin, species (S. dysenteriae, S. flexneri, S. sonnei, S. boydii)
Proteus — swarming motility, UTI, struvite stones, urease positive
Pseudomonas aeruginosa — pyocyanin, ecthyma gangrenosum, burn wound infections, CF lung infections, otitis externa
Vibrio cholerae — cholera toxin (ADP-ribosylation of Gs), rice-water stools, TCBS agar, string test, O1 & O139
Vibrio parahaemolyticus — Kanagawa phenomenon
Campylobacter jejuni — Guillain-Barré syndrome, bloody diarrhea
Helicobacter pylori — gastritis, peptic ulcer, gastric carcinoma, MALT lymphoma, urease test, CLO test
Yersinia pestis — plague (bubonic, pneumonic, septicemic), safety pin appearance
Brucella — undulant fever, Castaneda medium, serology
Legionella pneumophila — Legionnaires' disease, Pontiac fever, BCYE agar, urinary antigen test
Acinetobacter — MDR nosocomial infections

Mycobacterium tuberculosis — acid-fast staining (Ziehl-Neelsen), culture (LJ medium, BACTEC, MGIT), cord factor, tuberculin test (Mantoux), pathogenesis (Ghon complex, Ranke complex, miliary TB, TB meningitis)
Drug-resistant TB — MDR-TB, XDR-TB, DOTS strategy
Mycobacterium leprae — leprosy (tuberculoid vs lepromatous, borderline), lepromin test, ridley-jopling classification, WHO MDT
Atypical mycobacteria — Runyon classification, M. avium complex (MAC), M. marinum, M. kansasii, M. fortuitum
BCG vaccine — strain, uses, complications
Lab diagnosis of TB — smear, culture, CBNAAT/GeneXpert, IGRA, molecular methods

topics.topic: Bacteriology — Spirochetes, Rickettsia, Chlamydia & Mycoplasma (~20 questions)
subtopics: Treponema pallidum — syphilis (primary, secondary, tertiary — gumma, tabes dorsalis, Argyll Robertson pupil), congenital syphilis, dark-field microscopy, VDRL, RPR, FTA-ABS, TPHA
Borrelia — relapsing fever (B. recurrentis), Lyme disease (B. burgdorferi — erythema migrans, stages)
Leptospira — leptospirosis (Weil disease), dark-field, MAT
Rickettsia — epidemic typhus (R. prowazekii), endemic typhus (R. typhi), Rocky Mountain spotted fever (R. rickettsii), scrub typhus (Orientia tsutsugamushi), Weil-Felix reaction
Coxiella burnetii — Q fever, no Weil-Felix reaction
Chlamydia trachomatis — trachoma (serotypes A-C), genital infections (D-K), LGV (L1-L3), neonatal conjunctivitis & pneumonia
Chlamydia pneumoniae & Chlamydia psittaci
Mycoplasma pneumoniae — atypical pneumonia, cold agglutinins, Eaton agent
Ureaplasma urealyticum
General virology — structure (capsid, envelope, nucleic acid), classification (Baltimore), replication cycle, viral genetics (reassortment, recombination, antigenic shift & drift)

Herpesviruses — HSV-1 (oral herpes, encephalitis), HSV-2 (genital herpes, neonatal herpes), VZV (chickenpox, shingles), EBV (infectious mononucleosis, Burkitt lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, heterophile antibodies), CMV (congenital CMV, owl's eye inclusion), HHV-6 (roseola), HHV-8 (Kaposi sarcoma)
Adenovirus — pharyngoconjunctival fever, epidemic keratoconjunctivitis
Poxviruses — smallpox (variola), vaccinia, molluscum contagiosum
Papillomaviruses (HPV) — genital warts, cervical cancer (types 16, 18), HPV vaccine
Polyomaviruses — JC virus (PML), BK virus
Parvoviruses — B19 (erythema infectiosum/fifth disease, aplastic crisis, hydrops fetalis)
Hepatitis B virus — HBsAg, HBeAg, anti-HBc, serological markers, window period, chronic hepatitis, HCC, vaccine
Orthomyxoviruses — influenza (antigenic shift vs drift, H & N subtypes, avian flu, swine flu), oseltamivir
Paramyxoviruses — measles (Koplik spots, SSPE, giant cell pneumonia), mumps (parotitis, orchitis), RSV (bronchiolitis), parainfluenza (croup)
Rhabdovirus — rabies (Negri bodies, hydrophobia, post-exposure prophylaxis, vaccine)
Picornaviruses — poliovirus (poliomyelitis, Sabin vs Salk vaccine, AFP surveillance), coxsackievirus (hand-foot-mouth, herpangina, myocarditis), echovirus, rhinovirus, hepatitis A
Togaviruses — rubella (congenital rubella syndrome), chikungunya
Flaviviruses — dengue (hemorrhagic fever, shock syndrome, NS1 antigen), Zika, Japanese encephalitis, yellow fever, West Nile
Filoviruses — Ebola, Marburg
Bunyaviruses — hantavirus, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever
Arenaviruses — Lassa fever
Coronaviruses — SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19)
Retroviruses — HIV (structure, replication, CD4 tropism, viral load, ELISA, Western blot, p24 antigen, opportunistic infections, AIDS-defining illnesses, ART)
Rotavirus — infantile diarrhea, vaccine
Calicivirus — norovirus (gastroenteritis)
Hepatitis C virus — chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, HCC, DAAs
Hepatitis D (delta agent) & Hepatitis E (pregnancy)
General mycology — classification (yeasts, molds, dimorphic), fungal structure, KOH mount, culture (SDA)
Superficial mycoses — pityriasis versicolor (Malassezia furfur — spaghetti & meatball appearance), tinea nigra, piedra
Cutaneous mycoses (dermatophytosis) — Trichophyton, Microsporum, Epidermophyton; tinea corporis, capitis, pedis, cruris, unguium
Subcutaneous mycoses — sporotrichosis (Sporothrix schenckii — rose gardener), chromoblastomycosis (copper penny bodies), mycetoma (Madura foot)

Systemic mycoses — histoplasmosis (Histoplasma capsulatum — intracellular in macrophages), coccidioidomycosis (spherules), blastomycosis (broad-based budding), paracoccidioidomycosis (mariner's wheel)

Opportunistic mycoses — candidiasis (Candida albicans — germ tube test, pseudohyphae), cryptococcosis (Cryptococcus neoformans — India ink, capsule, latex agglutination), aspergillosis (Aspergillus fumigatus — septate hyphae, 45° branching, aspergilloma, ABPA, invasive), mucormycosis/zygomycosis (Rhizopus — aseptate/pauciseptate, 90° branching, rhinocerebral)
Pneumocystis jirovecii — PCP in AIDS, silver stain
Entamoeba histolytica — amoebic dysentery, liver abscess (anchovy sauce pus), flask-shaped ulcer, trophozoite with ingested RBCs, cyst morphology
Giardia lamblia — giardiasis, falling leaf motility, duodenal biopsy
Cryptosporidium — AIDS-related diarrhea, modified acid-fast stain

Plasmodium species — P. vivax (benign tertian, Schüffner dots, hypnozoites), P. falciparum (malignant tertian, Maurer clefts, cerebral malaria, blackwater fever), P. malariae (quartan), P. ovale, P. knowlesi
Malaria — life cycle (mosquito & human stages), diagnosis (peripheral smear, RDT, PCR), treatment, prophylaxis
Leishmania — visceral (kala-azar — L. donovani, LD bodies, splenic aspirate), cutaneous (L. tropica), mucocutaneous (L. braziliensis), Montenegro test
Trypanosoma — T. brucei (African sleeping sickness, Winterbottom sign, CSF examination), T. cruzi (Chagas disease, Romana sign, megacolon, megaesophagus)
Toxoplasma gondii — congenital toxoplasmosis, ring-enhancing lesions in AIDS, Sabin-Feldman dye test
Trichomonas vaginalis — vaginitis, strawberry cervix, wet mount
Free-living amoebae — Naegleria fowleri (PAM), Acanthamoeba (keratitis, GAE)

Cestodes (tapeworms) — Taenia solium (cysticercosis, neurocysticercosis), Taenia saginata, Echinococcus granulosus (hydatid cyst — Casoni test, daughter cysts), Hymenolepis nana (dwarf tapeworm), Diphyllobothrium latum (B12 deficiency)

Nematodes (roundworms) — Ascaris lumbricoides (Loeffler syndrome, biliary obstruction), Ancylostoma duodenale & Necator americanus (hookworm — iron deficiency anemia, ground itch), Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm — perianal pruritus, scotch tape test), Strongyloides stercoralis (hyperinfection in immunosuppressed, autoinfection), Trichuris trichiura (whipworm — rectal prolapse)

Tissue nematodes — Wuchereria bancrofti & Brugia malayi (lymphatic filariasis, elephantiasis, nocturnal periodicity, DEC), Onchocerca volvulus (river blindness, Mazzotti reaction), Loa loa (Calabar swelling, diurnal periodicity), Dracunculus medinensis (guinea worm)
Trichinella spiralis — trichinosis, encysted larvae in muscle

Trematodes (flukes) — Schistosoma (S. mansoni, S. japonicum, S. haematobium — bladder carcinoma), liver flukes (Fasciola hepatica, Clonorchis sinensis — cholangiocarcinoma), lung fluke (Paragonimus westermani), intestinal fluke (Fasciolopsis buski)
Larva migrans — cutaneous (Ancylostoma braziliense), visceral (Toxocara canis/cati)
Specimen collection & transport — blood culture, CSF, urine, stool, sputum, swabs
Microscopy — Gram stain, Ziehl-Neelsen, Albert stain, India ink, KOH mount, dark-field, fluorescence
Culture techniques — aerobic, anaerobic, CO2 enriched, cell culture (for viruses)
Biochemical tests — catalase, coagulase, oxidase, urease, indole, citrate, TSI, VP, methyl red
Serological tests — agglutination (Widal, Weil-Felix, Paul-Bunnell), precipitation, complement fixation, ELISA, Western blot, IFA
Molecular diagnostics — PCR, RT-PCR, GeneXpert, LAMP, sequencing
Antimicrobial susceptibility testing — disc diffusion, MIC, automated systems (VITEK)
Hospital infection control — nosocomial infections, hand hygiene, biomedical waste management, isolation precautions (standard, contact, droplet, airborne)
Emerging & re-emerging infections
